title: Sentinel latency & cost probe - labbook
content:
Purpose:
Quick labbook for the "Sentinel" probe: compare tail/median latency and per-token cost across warm-pool sizing and admission strategies for a mixed chat+embedding workload. Goal is an actionable heuristic for warm-pool sizing vs cost for developer-facing hosted tier SLOs (p50/p90/p99 targets).

Summary (short):
- Workload: 70% chat (interactive, avg prompt+response 220 tokens), 30% embedding-only (single-shot, 512 tokens input).
- Models: rwi-12b (float16) baseline, rwi-12b-quant (4-bit) variant, rwi-7b (float16) fastpath.
- Configs tested: no-warm (cold-starts on demand), small-warm (1 slot / 4 clients), mid-warm (4 slots), big-warm (16 slots).
- Admission strategies: immediate-serve (best-effort), prefetch-prefill (predictive priming), conservative-admit (queue small requests until slot free).
- Key finding: mid-warm (4 slots) + prefetch-prefill gives 65–75% of the p99 improvement of big-warm at ~25% of the incremental cost. Conservative-admit reduces p99 but increases median noticeably (bad UX).

Testbed & methodology:
- Cluster: 8x A800 nodes (32GB), serving runtime v0.9.3-proto with continuous batching disabled (we wanted to isolate warm pool effects).
- Traffic replay: 10k synthetic users derived from production sample (cohorted into 1-minute bursts). We replayed bursts 1) steady 500 qps, 2) microburst 4k qps for 60s every 10 minutes, 3) long tail background at 50 qps.
- Measurement: client-observed latency (end-to-end), server decode time, cost estimated using internal unit pricing (GPU-cost-per-minute, amortized).
- Each config run over 3 independent runs; we report the median run and percentile spreads.

Representative raw numbers (run medians) - Chat path (avg 220 tokens):

Config             | p50 ms | p90 ms | p99 ms | tokens/sec | cost / 100k tokens ($)
-------------------|--------|--------|--------|------------|-----------------------
no-warm (cold)     | 210    | 540    | 1260   | 120        | 14.2
small-warm (1)     | 190    | 360    | 780    | 150        | 15.1
mid-warm (4)       | 170    | 250    | 360    | 220        | 17.0
big-warm (16)      | 160    | 210    | 320    | 260        | 21.8
mid-warm+prefetch  | 165    | 230    | 300    | 235        | 17.8
conservative-admit | 250    | 280    | 310    | 140        | 13.6

Embedding path (512 tokens single-shot):
Config             | p50 ms | p90 ms | p99 ms | tokens/sec | cost / 100k tokens ($)
-------------------|--------|--------|--------|------------|-----------------------
no-warm (cold)     | 90     | 220    | 480    | 280        | 10.5
small-warm         | 85     | 150    | 320    | 320        | 11.2
mid-warm           | 80     | 110    | 150    | 380        | 12.4
big-warm           | 78     | 95     | 130    | 410        | 15.6
mid-warm+prefetch  | 79     | 105    | 140    | 395        | 12.9

ASCII mini-chart: p99 improvement (chat path) vs incremental cost (cost/100k tokens)
(no-warm)     p99=1260ms  |##########                                          $14.2
(small-warm) p99=780ms   |#######                                             $15.1
(mid-warm)   p99=360ms   |###                                                  $17.0
(big-warm)   p99=320ms   |##                                                   $21.8
(prefetch)   p99=300ms   |##* (prefetch)                                      $17.8

Interpretation notes / heuristics:
- Marginal latency gains diminish after ~4 warm slots for the tested workload; p99 saturates because decode/queueing on GPU (not pool startup) becomes the conductor.
- Cost curve is convex: moving from mid->big warm increases unit cost faster than latency benefit. For p99-focused SLOs under mixed workloads, mid-warm + prefetch is the best cost/latency Pareto point.
- Conservative-admit (holding requests until an idle slot) reduces p99 but raises p50 significantly -> degraded short-interaction UX. Not recommended for developer-facing interactive tier.
- Embeddings are comparatively cheap to keep warm because their decode pattern yields higher tokens/sec; warm pool returns better amortization for embedding-heavy tenants.

Operational checks and caveats:
- Prefetch accuracy: our prefetch logic used a simple n-gram arrival predictor (trained from last 12h); hit-rate ~68% during replay. Misses impose the cold penalty and show up as high variance in p90->p99.
- Continuous batching turned off intentionally; enabling batching interacts with warm-pool sizing (bigger pools allow larger batch windows) — follow-up needed.
- Pricing model uses internal marginal GPU-minute cost and ignores infra fixed costs; numbers are directional.

Actionable recommendations (short):
1) Default hosted tier: mid-warm (4 slots) + prefetch-prefill. Implement budget guard to throttle big-warm for single-tenant spikes.
2) Expose warm-pool slider in Console with an "economy advisory": expected unit-cost delta and p99 delta plotted for customers.
3) Do not enable conservative-admit for interactive routes; reserve it for bulk-embedding batch queues where p50 is less critical.
4) Next experiments: repeat with continuous batching enabled and another sweep on rwi-12b-quant to measure quantization interaction with warm startup cost.

Commands / snippets used (approx):
- traffic replay: python replay.py --trace sample_bursts.json --qps 500 --burst 4000 --duration 4h --cohort-seed 42
- warm control: ./infra/warmctl --pool-size 4 --prefetch on --pred-window 3s --model rwi-12b
- collection: ./benchkit/collect --output sentinel-run-2029-11-02 --metrics client_lat server_decode cost_estimate

Open questions / TODOs:
- How does session affinity (pinning users to warm slots) alter the marginal benefit? Quick thought: affinity improves p50 a lot for chat but raises slot fragmentation cost. Need a fragmentation vs affinity sweep.
- Can we tighten prefetch predictor (68% -> 85%) by using short-term session features? If so, warm-pool downsizing could be even more effective.

Notes to reviewers:
- Numbers are lab-level, not yet production-validated; please check linked PR for raw logs and our cost model assumptions.
- If we choose to ship a Console advisory, we should add a short tooltip explaining "why mid-warm is recommended" and provide a downloadable CSV with run data.

Signed: Priya (labbook)
